# Requirement diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-requirement/grammar/requirement.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Requirement diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `requirementDiagram`
diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4), with two lexer rules decided for v13 (spec #520): a blank run before a line end
ends at the line break (D431), and `direction` is read only at the start of a line (D432).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are matched without
regard to case.

Statements need no separator: `"a" - traces -> "b" "c" - traces -> "d"` is two relations. A
line break after blanks is read as one more blank inside a statement, as mermaid@12 read it,
and is a line break where one is needed.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A requirement diagram is `requirementDiagram` on a line of its own, then statements:
requirements, elements, relations, classes and styles, the direction and the accessible title
and description.

```ebnf
diagram = Header nl { statement | nl } EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = RD ;
```

```ebnf
nl = NEWLINE
   | NEWLINE_AFTER_BLANK ;
```

A line break after blanks inside a statement: read as one more blank (D431).

```ebnf
blank = [ NEWLINE_AFTER_BLANK ] ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Requirement
          | Element
          | Relation
          | Shorthand
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr
          | Direction nl
          | Style
          | ClassDef
          | Class ;
```

`requirement name { … }`, or one of `functionalRequirement`, `interfaceRequirement`,
`performanceRequirement`, `physicalRequirement` and `designConstraint`: a requirement box. The
`{` ends its line; each field, and the `}`, is on a line of its own.

```ebnf
Requirement @Requirement = requirementKind blank name blank [ STYLE_SEPARATOR blank idList blank ] STRUCT_START nl { requirementField | nl } STRUCT_STOP ;
```

```ebnf
requirementKind = REQUIREMENT
                | FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENT
                | INTERFACE_REQUIREMENT
                | PERFORMANCE_REQUIREMENT
                | PHYSICAL_REQUIREMENT
                | DESIGN_CONSTRAINT ;
```

`id: …`, `text: …`, `risk: low|medium|high` and `verifymethod:
analysis|demonstration|inspection|test`. A repeated field keeps its first value.

```ebnf
requirementField = ID blank COLONSEP blank name nl
                 | TEXT blank COLONSEP blank name nl
                 | RISK blank COLONSEP blank risk nl
                 | VERIFYMTHD blank COLONSEP blank method nl ;
```

```ebnf
risk = LOW_RISK
     | MED_RISK
     | HIGH_RISK ;
```

```ebnf
method = VERIFY_ANALYSIS
       | VERIFY_DEMONSTRATION
       | VERIFY_INSPECTION
       | VERIFY_TEST ;
```

`element name { … }`: an element box, with the fields `type: …` and `docref: …`.

```ebnf
Element @Element = ELEMENT blank name blank [ STYLE_SEPARATOR blank idList blank ] STRUCT_START nl { elementField | nl } STRUCT_STOP ;
```

```ebnf
elementField = TYPE blank COLONSEP blank name nl
             | DOCREF blank COLONSEP blank name nl ;
```

```ebnf
name = unqString
     | qString ;
```

`a - satisfies -> b` or `b <- satisfies - a`: a relation from `a` to `b`, of the kinds
`contains`, `copies`, `derives`, `satisfies`, `verifies`, `refines` and `traces`.

```ebnf
Relation @Relation = name blank LINE blank relationship blank END_ARROW_R blank name
                   | name blank END_ARROW_L blank relationship blank LINE blank name ;
```

```ebnf
relationship = CONTAINS
             | COPIES
             | DERIVES
             | SATISFIES
             | VERIFIES
             | REFINES
             | TRACES ;
```

`name:::class,…`: gives a box classes (as `class` does).

```ebnf
Shorthand @Class = name blank STYLE_SEPARATOR blank idList ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = acc_title acc_title_value ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description of the diagram.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = acc_descr acc_descr_value
                   | acc_descr_multiline_value ;
```

`direction LR`: the layout direction, on a line of its own.

```ebnf
Direction @Direction = direction_tb
                     | direction_bt
                     | direction_rl
                     | direction_lr ;
```

`style name,… fill:#f9f,stroke:#333`: styles boxes defined before it.

```ebnf
Style @Style = STYLE blank idList blank styles ;
```

`classDef name,… fill:#f9f,color:#000`: defines classes of styles.

```ebnf
ClassDef @ClassDef = CLASSDEF blank idList blank styles ;
```

`class name,… class,…`: gives boxes defined before it classes.

```ebnf
Class @Class = CLASS blank idList blank idList ;
```

```ebnf
idList = idItem { blank COMMA blank idItem } ;
```

```ebnf
idItem = ALPHA
       | name ;
```

```ebnf
styles = style { blank COMMA blank style } ;
```

```ebnf
style = styleComponent { blank styleComponent } ;
```

```ebnf
styleComponent = ALPHA
               | COLON
               | BRKT
               | MINUS
               | SEMICOLON ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `string`, `style`, `acc_title`, `acc_descr`, `acc_descr_multiline`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | title | `title\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `title …` is read, but no statement takes it: a requirement diagram has no title statement; set `title` in the front matter. |
| INITIAL | acc_title | `accTitle\s*:\s*` | push(acc_title) | `accTitle: …` and `accDescr: …` take the rest of the line; `accDescr { … }` runs to `}`. |
| acc_title | acc_title_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | acc_descr | `accDescr\s*:\s*` | push(acc_descr) |  |
| acc_descr | acc_descr_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | — | `accDescr\s*\{\s*` | push(acc_descr_multiline) |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | — | `\}` | pop |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | acc_descr_multiline_value | `[^}]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | direction_tb | `(?<=(?:^\|\n)[^\S\n]*)direction[^\S\n\r  ]+TB\b` |  | `direction TB`, `BT`, `LR` or `RL`, at the start of a line (D432). |
| INITIAL | direction_bt | `(?<=(?:^\|\n)[^\S\n]*)direction[^\S\n\r  ]+BT\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | direction_rl | `(?<=(?:^\|\n)[^\S\n]*)direction[^\S\n\r  ]+RL\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | direction_lr | `(?<=(?:^\|\n)[^\S\n]*)direction[^\S\n\r  ]+LR\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\n+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `(?<=(?:^\|\n)[^\S\n]*)\s+` |  | Blanks at the start of a line are skipped, blank lines with them. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE_AFTER_BLANK | `[^\S\n]+\n+` |  | Blanks after other text on a line, then the line break (D431): a line break of its own kind. |
| INITIAL | — | `[^\S\n]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `#[^\n]*` |  | `#` or `%` at the start of a token begins a comment to the end of the line. |
| INITIAL | — | `%[^\n]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |
| INITIAL | RD | `requirementDiagram\b` |  | `requirementDiagram`: starts a requirement diagram, on a line of its own. |
| INITIAL | STRUCT_START | `\{` |  |  |
| INITIAL | STRUCT_STOP | `\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | STYLE_SEPARATOR | `:::` |  | `name:::class`: gives a box a class, as `class name class` does. |
| INITIAL | COLONSEP | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ID | `id\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | TEXT | `text\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RISK | `risk\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFYMTHD | `verifyMethod\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | REQUIREMENT | `requirement\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENT | `functionalRequirement\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | INTERFACE_REQUIREMENT | `interfaceRequirement\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | PERFORMANCE_REQUIREMENT | `performanceRequirement\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | PHYSICAL_REQUIREMENT | `physicalRequirement\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DESIGN_CONSTRAINT | `designConstraint\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LOW_RISK | `low\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | MED_RISK | `medium\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | HIGH_RISK | `high\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFY_ANALYSIS | `analysis\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFY_DEMONSTRATION | `demonstration\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFY_INSPECTION | `inspection\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFY_TEST | `test\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ELEMENT | `element\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | CONTAINS | `contains\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COPIES | `copies\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DERIVES | `derives\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | SATISFIES | `satisfies\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | VERIFIES | `verifies\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | REFINES | `refines\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | TRACES | `traces\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | TYPE | `type\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DOCREF | `docref\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | STYLE | `style\b` | push(style) | Styles: `style`, `classDef` and `class` read the rest of the line as names and styles; spaces between them are dropped. |
| style | ALPHA | `\w+` |  |  |
| style | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| style | SEMICOLON | `;` |  |  |
| style | PERCENT | `%` |  | `%` in a style is read, but no style takes it. |
| style | MINUS | `-` |  |  |
| style | BRKT | `#` |  |  |
| style | — | ` ` |  |  |
| style | — | `"` | push(string) |  |
| style | — | `\n` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | CLASSDEF | `classDef\b` | push(style) |  |
| INITIAL | CLASS | `class\b` | push(style) |  |
| INITIAL | END_ARROW_L | `<-` |  | Relations: `a - satisfies -> b`, or `b <- satisfies - a`. |
| INITIAL | END_ARROW_R | `->` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LINE | `-` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `"` | push(string) | A quoted name or text: `"…"`, line breaks included, no escapes. |
| string | — | `"` | pop |  |
| string | qString | `[^"]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | unqString | `[\w][^:,\r\n\{\<\>\-\=]*` |  | An unquoted name or text: up to `:`, `,`, `{`, `<`, `>`, `-`, `=` or the line end, blanks off both ends. |
| * | ALPHA | `\w+` |  |  |
| * | NUM | `[0-9]+` |  | Never read: `\w+` comes first in every mode. |
| * | COMMA | `,` |  |  |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
